expectation: Membrane or cytoplasmic rings on irregular or ramified macrophages, a subset of the CD68+/IBA1+ cells. Common in intestinal lamina propria and submucosa, scattered singly or in small groups beneath the epithelium and around vessels. Absent from epithelium.
observed: A: discrete yellow dots concentrated in the mucosa/lamina propria of the folds, plus fine grain over the outer wall. B: ring-shaped membranous cells clustered top left, and one bright blob. C: a single small cell. D: an irregular macrophage-like cell. E1: membrane rings in IBA1-dense stroma; IBA1 is saturated in E2/E3, so the merge shows little.
why: Clear membrane-ring cells with macrophage shapes cluster in the mucosal stroma, separate from the epithelium and from the background grain, which is how a CD163 subset should look.
notes: Membrane-ringed, irregular CD163+ cells sit in the lamina propria (B top left, D, E1). There is some fine grain over the outer wall, and the brightest blobs look like artefacts. IBA1 is saturated, so row E adds little.
